newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-WORLD CUP HOSTS REACH LAST EIGHT IN CONTRASTING MOODS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WORLD CUP HOSTS REACH LAST EIGHT IN CONTRASTING MOODS.

text.p: Defending champions Japan enter the knockout stage of the Asian Cup on Sunday in confident mood while South Korea, their bitter regional rivals and co-hosts of the 2002 World Cup, will need to improve.
Japan are the only team in the competition with a 100 percent record and have thoroughly justified their ranking as tournament favourites.

After struggling in their opening match against Syria, when they had to fight back from 1-0 down with two goals in the last six minutes, they produced some fine, measured football in beating Uzbekistan 4-0 and China 1-0.
Promising youngster Masakiyo Maezono and striker Takuya Takagi were both exceptional in the group matches and the Japanese are expected to overcome Kuwait in Sunday's quarter-final in Al-Ain.

In contrast, South Korea struggled to qualify for the last eight of the 12-nation competition, drawing with hosts United Arab Emirates, then beating Indonesia before going down to a surprise 2-0 defeat by Kuwait.
The Koreans, twice Asian Cup winners and runners-up on three other occasions, face Iran in their quarter-final in Dubai on Monday.
UAE play Iraq on Sunday and Saudi Arabia, beaten finalists last time around, take on China on Monday in the other two quarter-finals, both of which are to be played in Abu Dhabi.
The draw has kept Gulf foes Iraq and Kuwait apart -- at least for the time being.
But the Asian Football Confederation will have a problem on their hands if Kuwait upset Japan and Iraq beat the hosts in Sunday's quarter-finals, the winners facing each other in the semifinals.
Kuwait has said it would pull out of the tournament rather than play its former occupier.
